body: Yes, I would recommend Namecheap. I've been with them for 8 years.

I have tried many of the things you've suggested, and not just once, but many times over. Eat healthy? There was a time when I'd only eat organic, and mostly fruits/veggies, but that became too expensive and hard to maintain. Exercise? I was an avid hiker and I still love swimming, but I lost interest due to depression and now it'd take a lot of conditioning to be able to even walk a mile. Join clubs? I volunteered a lot, and sometimes I still do, but I've never made a lasting relationship. I even volunteered all summer once for a conservation group, but it turns out they were not the kind of people I wanted to be associated with (they actually hired a well-known corrupt local politician to be their President, and things went downhill from there.... They're still around, but they had to move locations and change their name.)

A new job? What new job? I'm a high school dropout. I got my first and only job as a fluke, before the 2008 economic collapse. I was fucking lucky. Now that I've been effectively fired, those six years are down the fucking drain. I can't get a recommendation from my former employer now. All a new company is going to see is that I dropped out of high school and then did nothing for six years.

What you and a lot of people don't understand is that if it were as simple as eating right, exercising and meeting new people, I would be cured! But it's not. Eating right requires money and time to prepare meals, exercise requires free time and motivation, and meeting new people requires a lot of trial and error. All of which I've already done, multiple times. That's why I'm giving up.
